speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how are soft skills inculcated, nurtured and evaluated in our education system; (b) how is the impact of e-learning and digitalisation on soft skills acquisition being assessed; and (c) what measures are being taken to ensure that soft skills continue to be learned amidst COVID-19 safe distancing measures including in higher education.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These competencies are developed through both curricular and co-curricular activities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, through group work, students learn communication and collaboration skills and how to manage relationships with peers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In learning humanities, students develop stronger global awareness and cross-cultural understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In learning sciences, students are exposed to the inquiry process and inventive thinking of scientists.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the classroom, co-curricular and Values-in-Action activities are platforms that enable students to deepen their mastery of 21CC through rich and authentic learning opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, the IHLs are enhancing their curriculum to provide students with more multi-disciplinary and inter-disciplinary exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help broaden students’ perspectives and encourage trans-disciplinary thinking and approaches to problem-solving.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In recent times, with greater use of technology and digital platforms, soft skills can be nurtured through online and offline learning experiences that reinforce each other.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, students learn interpersonal and collaboration skills through both in-person group work and through the use of online collaboration tools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: IHLs have also progressively increased the number of students allowed back on campus for in-person learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOE is taking incremental steps to resume more of such in-person activities safely in schools and IHLs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to help ensure that our students and graduates are future-ready by progressively developing their soft skills at each stage of the education journey.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, how are students who need extra development in soft skills identified?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The second question, Mr Speaker, if I may ask the Minister, what measures are being taken to ensure that students from less advantaged backgrounds, students who are starting with less, that these students continue to have good opportunities to build social networks, to build social capital and to develop soft skills in a variety of domains?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I raise this, Mr Speaker, because there is a good body of evidence from researchers such as David Deming or Catherine Weinberger on the role of soft skills synergising with technical skills.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And this is all the more important today in our uncharted new 21st century COVID-19 world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This applies, of course, to their mastery of subjects, but it also applies to soft skills.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, students that may benefit from more coaching when it comes to communication skills – that is something that the teachers would really be able to identify and they can provide more help, be it through their lessons in class or by giving them more opportunities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The importance of the 21CC, which I highlighted just now, is integral to the teaching and learning process in schools.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The school leaders and educators are fully aware of this and will continue to make sure they identify students who are weaker, who will need more help and can benefit from more help.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Certainly, we will continue to try to do better at this – provide more systematic uplifting programmes, more exposure, more opportunities for these students.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We already allocate more resources to help these students.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We make sure that there are more programmes in place to help these students and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I would say that this effort cannot be done by schools alone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also need help from the community, we need help from industry, so that together, we can provide maximum opportunities to help students who can benefit from such help.
